texts: bad: 'Keepers cannot explain X' states an ability of a whole kind, which must be recorded as a property of the keeper kind — and that property's action slot can only hold a bare kind, so 'the moon-phase rule' as one particular rule has nowhere to live; the parse instead produced a per-keeper event rule carrying 'can', the one shape the instruction set rules out for a modal claim over a kind, so the sentence's only predication is mis-recorded either way. Put the specific rule in subject position and leave the keepers as the agent: "The moon-phase rule cannot be explained by keepers." That is an ordinary denied-ability event: the definite rule keeps its own symbol as the thing not explained, the inability is preserved at strength 0, and no kind-level property form is needed. (If the rule need not stay definite, 'Keepers cannot explain moon-phase rules.' also parses cleanly, at the cost of generalising away the particular rule.)
